newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler expects marked DASA sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Daimler expects marked DASA sales growth.

text.p: German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG said on Wednesday it expected revenues from its Dasa aerospace business to "grow markedly" in 1997 after a major reorganisation of the business in 1995.
Daimler said it expected the earnings power of Dasa to again improve in the operational area due to the reorganisation and also due to the stronger dollar.
"We expect revenues in the aerospace business to grow markedly in 1997, above all because of the pleasing development of orders in the commerical jet sector," Daimler said in its 1996 annual report.
The report, released at the Stuttgart-based group's annual news conference, said Daimler's MTU aircraft engine unit would also profit from the revival in the commercial jet market.

Daimler's Dasa unit reported 1996 sales of 13.1 billion marks ($7.6 billion), down from 15.1 billion marks in 1995 when it took a 2.3 billion-mark charge to rid itself of troubled aircraft maker Fokker of the Netherlands.

Daimler said revenues at its space systems unit would likely increase due to new major projects and that its defence and civil systems unit counted on a "slight growth" in sales due to "an emerging upturn" in defence-sector business.
